link.reason: About the T-pillar or three-doorway design on the back of the Gate of the Sun. The Viracocha mirror-civilization story is about Viracocha holding condors, not this carving.

candidates.title: Offset orientation of the Susi temples as a dating clue
candidates.quote: temples they faced either west or east but not anymore they're offset

link.reason: The same claim: the Susi temples once faced east or west and are now offset, which points to a change in the axis.
link.difference: Frames the offset explicitly as a dating clue.

candidates.title: Haldi as celestial intelligence rather than ancient aliens
candidates.quote: has been a bit skewed from what I look at with these Gods like haldi it seems more like some kind of celestial intelligence

link.reason: Reads Haldi as a celestial intelligence rather than an ancient alien. The Haldi-spearhead story is about archaeologists reading the relief as a spearhead, which is a different claim.

candidates.title: Eleusinian mysteries as near-death rituals
candidates.quote: because if you look at the linian Mysteries or any of these other rituals they involve the temporary killing of the physical body through a near-death experience

link.reason: A general claim that Eleusis and other rituals temporarily killed the body through a near-death experience. The kykeon and Minoan-forms stories make other claims about Eleusis, and this one is wider than either.

candidates.title: Documentary project with secret dating evidence
candidates.quote: I am part of a very significant documentary that I'm leading

link.reason: Matt's own 2024 documentary project with secret dating evidence. No story covers it.

candidates.title: Antikythera mechanism
candidates.quote: the anti theor mechanism you know that was found on this island in Greece

link.reason: The same ancient Greek astronomical mechanism found at Antikythera, told by the same host.
link.difference: Places the find on a Greek island rather than in a shipwreck, and cites Forbidden Archaeology.

candidates.title: Hancock–Dibble debate and the shipwreck data
candidates.quote: you can see Graham Hancock debate flint dible and then you can fact checked Flint Dibble and realized that he got all his shipwreck data completely wrong

link.reason: The Hancock–Dibble debate and a fact-check of Dibble's shipwreck data. No story covers it.

candidates.title: Ancient temples dismantled and items removed
candidates.quote: certain ancient temples that have been dismantled and things that have been removed and I have found very very compelling evidence that that it's happened

link.reason: A claim that ancient temples in the Lake Van region were dismantled and items removed. No story covers it.

candidates.title: Only about 150 of 40,000 Ashurbanipal tablets translated
candidates.quote: the 40,000 Ki form tablets at the Asher Bop Paul Library around 150 have been translated out of 40,000

link.reason: About how few of the Ashurbanipal tablets have been translated. The nearest story is Layard's 1848 excavation of the library, which is a different event.

candidates.title: Schliemann finds Troy
candidates.quote: Hinrich V schlaman in 18 71 being motivated by thus cities and Homer everybody was saying that was just mythology and then he finds Troy

link.reason: Both tell of Heinrich Schliemann taking Homer seriously and finding Troy in Turkey; the teller is the same host.
link.difference: Gives the year 1871 and says everyone dismissed Troy as mythology.

candidates.title: Plato's account of Athens fighting Atlantis 9,000 years before
candidates.quote: you know um uh Plato saying you know at tus and crus you know this in this at this Mythos Festival saying that 9,000 years ago we fought against Atlantis the Athenians did

link.reason: Both tell Plato's account in the Timaeus and Critias of ancient Athens fighting a war against Atlantis.
link.difference: Puts the war 9,000 years back and mentions the festival setting; credits only Plato.

candidates.title: Plutarch names Sonchis, priest at Sais
candidates.quote: in plutar he describes how there was a very specific Elder priest at the Temple of C in Egypt named sanas

link.reason: The nearest story is Solon being told the Atlantis story by the priests at Sais. This telling is a narrower claim: Plutarch's text names one particular elder priest, Sonchis. That makes it a distinct document claim.

candidates.title: Plutarch names Sonchis, elder priest of the Temple of Sais, as Solon's source for the Atlantis story
